data.long_meaning: Behrouz is a Persian name derived from the Persian word 'Bahra' meaning 'lord' or 'master'. In Islamic context, it can be interpreted as 'the one who has the power and authority'. The name Behrouz carries the meaning “Lord, Master” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Behrouz usually hope their child will grow to embody lord, master and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Behrouz was a Persian warrior who fought in the army of the Sassanid Emperor Khosrow II during the Byzantine-Sassanid War in the 7th century. He was renowned for his bravery and was the commander of the left wing of the Persian army during the Battle of Nineveh. After a failed Byzantine siege, Behrouz led a successful counterattack and killed the Byzantine Emperor Heraclius' brother Theodosius. However, he was later killed in the Battle of Jalula during the same war.

Behrouz was also a Persian hero in the Shia tradition, who was allegedly the standard-bearer of Imam Ali during the Battle of Jamal in 657 AD. According to Shia sources, Behrouz fought bravely against Aqeel ibn Abi Talib, the governor of Kufa on behalf of Muawiya I, and was ultimately killed by Aqeel.
